description: Agent protocol (L3, crate fgos-agent-protocol): one pure state machine per CLI x launch mode. It reads what the agent shows and names what happened; it never opens a tab, picks a model, changes a timeout or decides a retry. It does not build argv: argv comes from the executor configuration through resolveExecutorCommand (src/runner/dispatch/transport.mjs) and is written into the envelope (owner decision 2026-10-16).

io.description: Port the supervisor wires to the adapter: terminal-control by key (terminal, 6.3). The direct mode reads no port: its adapter is handed the exit and the capture tail.

screen.output: string, the whole visible screen right now

output.state: string or null (idle, working, blocked, done)
output.matchedRule: boolean, a screen rule vouched for the verdict
output.promptText: string, the composer text the rule saw

inspect.meaning: the multiplexer's own agent detection for the pane (terminal-control inspect with detail); never a guess of the supervisor

clock.output: now_ms (monotonic) and pause(ms); every wait of an adapter goes through them so a vector can run on a virtual clock

results.ready: terminal: the CLI shows an empty prompt and can take the brief

blocked.meaning: the CLI waits for something only a person can do, or its provider refused the round (provider-error: an HTTP 4xx/5xx other than 401/403/429, from the last JSON event in direct mode or an `api error (<status>)` line on a terminal screen; usage-limit also covers a 429 or a `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` error body, from the same two places and from an omp give-up whose reason is a 429)

results.delivered: terminal: the brief is confirmed submitted (not merely visible)
results.delivery-unknown: terminal: could not confirm; never resend blind

completed.meaning: the agent finished and its result file exists

results.needs-human: the agent asked a question in its result or output that only a person can answer

exited.meaning: the agent process exited without a result file

directAdapter.inputs: envelope.launch (briefPath, outboxDir, capture paths), the agent exit reported by gate-exit, and the capture tail
decides: activity source for idle: growth of the stdout capture (any new text, a JSON event line included)
completion: agent exited and outbox/result-<N>.json exists -> completed; exited without it -> exited(code) unless a blocked/needs-human pattern was read

named blocked results from known output patterns on the stderr tail (login prompt, usage limit), and usage-limit or provider-error from the stdout tail's last JSON event (stopReason error: an errorStatus of 429 or a `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` error body is usage-limit; an errorStatus of 4xx/5xx other than 401/403 is provider-error)
the supervisor puts a blocked result in the receipt's `reason` as `direct:blocked:<reason>` (only for a non-zero exit with no outbox result); the settle step maps it to an outcome

providerSignal.meaning: a pure read of the CLI's last words that adds facts to a stop already named; never a verdict. None when no field is found. Direct: Direct::provider_signal(stderrTail, stdoutTail) over the same 5-line tails and last-event rule as classify; terminal: Terminal::stop_signal(screen) over the bottom 12 lines

fields.resetHint: string of at most 80 characters, the matched `resets in <dur>` or `try again at <h:mm am|pm>` phrase

providerSignal.wire: camelCase keys, a field not found is left out

matrix.unknownCli: direct: an unknown CLI gets the generic adapter name, and its last words are read for a dead login or a used-up quota like any other (an executor can wrap any program); terminal: an envelope naming a CLI without a terminal adapter is refused before launch (agent-protocol-unsupported)

vectors: an optional `expectSignal` on a vector asserts the provider signal; fixtures per cell live under packages/agent-protocol/contracts/fixtures/<mode>/<cli>/vectors.json (direct and terminal cells exist; terminal vectors replay recorded screens on a virtual clock)
